Table : delete_rows

Table_DeleteRows.Rd

Delete rows from a table given a query or a data frame to select rows. The query at a minimum must select the ROW_ID and ROW_VERSION columns. If you want to inspect the data that will be deleted ahead of time you may use the synQuery() function to get the data. The data frame must at least contain the ROW_ID and ROW_VERSION columns. And ROW_ETAG column is also required if the entity is one of the following: EntityView, Dataset, DatasetCollection, or SubmissionView. If both query and df are provided, the query will be used.

Usage

synDeleteRows(instance, query=NULL, df=NULL, job_timeout=600L, synapse_client=NULL)

Arguments

instance

(Table) The Table instance to operate on.

query

(Optional[str]) The query to select the rows to delete. The query at a minimum must select the ROW_ID and ROW_VERSION columns. See this document that describes the expected syntax of the query: <https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/org/sagebionetworks/repo/web/controller/TableExamples.html>

df

(Optional[data.frame]) A data frame that contains the rows to delete. The data frame must at least contain the ROW_ID and ROW_VERSION columns. If the entity is one of the following: EntityView, Dataset, DatasetCollection, or SubmissionView then the data frame must also contain the ROW_ETAG column. See this document that describes the expected columns of the data frame: <https://rest-docs.synapse.org/rest/org/sagebionetworks/repo/model/table/Row.html>

job_timeout

(int) The amount of time to wait for table updates to complete before a timeout error is thrown. The default is 600 seconds.

synapse_client

(Optional[Synapse]) If not passed in, the last created instance from the Synapse class constructor will be used.

Value

The results of your query or data frame for the rows that were deleted from the table.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Example 1: Selecting a row to delete
    # This example shows how you may select a row to delete from a table.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    # Also works with Dataset
    Table(id = "syn1234") |> synDeleteRows(query = "SELECT ROW_ID, ROW_VERSION FROM syn1234 WHERE foo = 'asdf'")

## Example 2: Selecting all rows that contain a null value
    # This example shows how you may select a row to delete from a table where
    # a column has a null value.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    # Also works with Dataset
    Table(id = "syn1234") |> synDeleteRows(query = "SELECT ROW_ID, ROW_VERSION FROM syn1234 WHERE foo is null")

## Example 3: Selecting rows to delete using a data frame
    # This example shows how you may select a row to delete from a table based on a data frame.
    library(synapser)
    synLogin()

    # Creating a data frame that contains the rows to delete.
    # In this example, we create a data frame that specifies the first two rows of the table for deletion.
    # Assuming no changes have been made to the table so the ROW_VERSION is 1L.

    df = data.frame(ROW_ID = c(1L, 2L), ROW_VERSION = c(1L, 1L  ))
    Table(id = "syn1234") |> synDeleteRows(df = df)
} # }
